prompt_text: I want to sell my house in Pleasanton. Which specific real estate agents should I call, and why?
q1_prompt_text: Who is the best real estate agent in Pleasanton CA to sell my house?
answer_verbatim:
I can give you specific agent names — but first I need a couple quick details so I pull the right local choices. Which Pleasanton do you mean (Pleasanton, CA is most common)? And please tell me:

- Your property’s address or at least the neighborhood/zip  
- Estimated list price or bedroom/bathroom/lot type (single-family, condo, etc.)  
- Your top priorities (max price, speed, lowest commission, hands-off, sell “as-is,” etc.)

If you don’t want to share those, here’s a practical plan now plus exactly which kinds of agents to call and why — so you can start contacting candidates today.

Which agents you should call (types, and why)
1. A top-producing Pleasanton listing agent who sells in your price range
   - Why: they have proven marketing systems, local buyer networks, and better likelihood of getting above-list offers.
   - How to find: look for agents with multiple recent sales in your subdivision (MLS, Zillow, Redfin, or “Sold” signs in neighborhood). Ask for recent comparable sales and their list-to-sale price ratio.

2. A hyper-local neighborhood specialist
   - Why: they know nuances of your specific street/school district and can target buyers who want your neighborhood; often better at pricing and staging for your micro-market.
   - How to find: check neighborhood Facebook groups, Nextdoor, or look up agents who list many homes on your block.

3. A high-volume team from a major brokerage (Compass, Keller Williams, Coldwell Banker, RE/MAX)
   - Why: big teams have broader advertising budgets, professional photographers, in-house transaction coordinators and mortgage/relocation pipelines.
   - How to find: company pages list their top teams and sales stats.

4. A discount or flat-fee MLS/limited service option (if cost matters)
   - Why: lower commission if you are comfortable handling some tasks (showings, negotiation). Good for a clearly priced, easy-to-show property.
   - How to find: search “flat fee MLS Pleasanton” or discount brokerages — but vet reviews carefully.

What to ask on first call (quick script)
- “How many homes like mine have you sold in Pleasanton in the last 12 months?”  
- “What was your average list-to-sale price ratio and average days on market?”  
- “Can you send two recent comps and a sample marketing plan you would use for my home?”  
- “What’s your total fee and any extra costs (staging, photography, lockbox)?”  
- “How do you communicate (phone/text/email) and how often will I get updates?”  

How to evaluate their answers
- Ask for specifics (addresses, sale prices, dates). Vague promises without data = red flag.  
- Prefer agents who provide a clear CMA, a timeline, and a concrete marketing plan (professional photos, online syndication, targeted outreach).  
- Look at reviews on Google, Zillow, Yelp; check past clients’ comments about communication and negotiation.

Next steps I can do for you
- If you give me the address or zip and your goals (price range, timeline), I will pull a short list (3–5) of top local agents in Pleasanton with reasons for each (recent comps, specialties, typical fees) and a suggested phone/email script to contact them.  

Which option would you prefer?
